source_ambiguities.description: The ascendant-OR-fourth rule and the subsequent specific fourth-house alternatives both appear in print. Neither replaces the other.

The second-house paragraph moves from personal alternatives to being within someone's power and recovery by money without explicitly restating the subject or object. Preserve that uncertainty while retaining the power relationship.
The fourth-house paragraph visibly ends a line with 'Labou-' and the following line begins 'of the Land'. The missing word completion is not securely supplied by this image.
The fifth-house masculine-sign parenthesis follows the son-or-daughter-of-cousin-or-nephew alternatives. Its grammatical reach is not explicitly settled.

The seventh-house feminine-sign condition follows the market buyer-or-seller alternative and precedes the enemy assertion. Preserve its position and the printed warning 'This must be warily understood'; do not relocate the condition to harmonize the paragraph.

The eleventh-house paragraph leaves the scope of 'or Neighbour' open and uses the awkward construction 'of the Houshold of the Querent his Mother'. Preserve the wording rather than asserting additional relationships.

The thief-significator distance scale names the ascendant lord in the fixed branch but the ascendant in the common and movable branches. Its movable branch counts terrestrial houses. The separate ascending-sign scale instead assigns half a mile per house when movable. Retain both scales and their differing endpoints and units.
The margin prints 'These judgments best agree from the Country'. Retain the unusual preposition without silently converting it into a precise geographical restriction.

The earlier general angular-placement rule says the thief remains in town, whereas this page distinguishes strong-angular remaining from weak-angular departure and separately gives the square-to-ascendant-lord rule. No precedence or reconciliation is printed.

In the sixth-lord paragraph, the word before 'any of their Lords' resembles 'will' or 'with'. Preserve the uncertain connective; do not invent an aspect, reception, conjunction or application condition.
The margin explicitly associates 'sometimes' with the willing return of goods. Whether it additionally qualifies the adjacent arrival-before-the-querent prediction is uncertain.

The direction methods attributed to others remain separate from the author's preference for the stronger of the significator and Moon. The pronoun in 'to whom he doth apply, or render his power' is not fully resolved, and rendering power is not defined here.
The Taurus glyph is followed by 'in the South against the east', then 'and so of the rest'. Preserve this wording and do not supply a precise bearing or an absent twelve-sign table.

The house-location paragraph first uses the thief's significator, then explicitly assigns the Sun to the house and Moon to its door. These distinct actors must remain distinct; their rules are not unified by the source.

source_completeness: Fully read the original images PDF377–381, printed pp343–347, in page order, including body text, printed marginal notes, every subsection heading, running heads, glyphs and catchwords; then read the original errata image before opening CANDIDATE.json. Checked every field of D001–D065 against the images. No additional omissions were identified beyond those listed. No appearance/name table or explicit reception rule appears on these five body pages. The eighth-house paragraph crosses PDF377–378, the town-departure paragraph crosses PDF378–379, and the degree-distance paragraph crosses PDF379–380; their visible continuations were included. PDF381 contains both omitted house/mark and door sections; the door paragraph continues beyond the supplied window. Same-volume printed errata includes p335, last line, 'Planets', and p336, lines 4 and 9, 'vertue'; no entry for p337 or pp343–347 was identified. These errata are distinct from body print and do not amend this window. Handwritten numbers and notes were not treated as Lilly's printed assertions. Physical overlap was reviewed for source content without judging ledger counts. The source's personal and criminal allegations supply no evidence about actual persons, and no modern criminal or clinical conclusions are drawn. No files were edited.
